events.title: Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) Quarterly Newsletter - Q2 & Q3 2026
events.summary: Country: Somalia Source: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs Please refer to the attached file. SHF News Allocations In the second and third quarters of 2026, the Somalia Humanitarian Fund (SHF) undertook three critical allocations to address urgent humanitarian needs. In July 2026, the SHF allocated US$ 2 million to scale up response required to mitigate the risk of famine in rural areas of Buurhakaba, Bay Region. The allocation prioritized multisectoral lifesaving assistance to increase access to food, integrated health, nutrition, and protection (GBV) services; and improve access to water. The allocation was complemented by a $10 million CERF Rapid Response grant to sustain humanitarian assistance to mitigate the adverse effects of the prolonged drought conditions in additional areas. In anticipation of a forecast Super El Nino, CERF granted an additional $7 million to facilitate timely, targeted, multi-sectoral interventions in flood high-risk districts along the Juba and Shabelle river basins. Given the gravity of the humanitarian situation amid continuing funding shortfalls, SHF also launched a $21 million Standard Allocation in September to provide integrated multisectoral assistance across seven priority districts hosting underserved communities with the highest severity of needs, including heightened protection and flood risks. Some $13 million from this envelope targeted flood -prone locations. The collective allocation of $33 million from CERF and SHF enabled the strategic use of limited resources through geographic and sectoral convergence, and sectoral complementarity to deliver much needed assistance to vulnerable communities.

Fiji has one of the fastest-growing HIV epidemics globally, with new infections rising approximately twelvefold between 2010 and 2025 . Dr Tedros made the announcement during his visit to the country to reinforce WHO’s support for a health system under severe pressure from the ongoing humanitarian and security crisis. The funding will provide equipment to the overwhelmed Hôpital Universitaire La Paix (HUP) in the capital, Port-au-Prince, including a computed tomography (CT) scanner and equipment for four operating rooms. HUP is the last major public referral hospital still operating in Port-au-Prince, a city where half (49.5%) of health facilities are non-functional and just 12% are partially operational. Across Haiti, a country of more than 11 million people, almost one quarter (24.5%) of health facilities are not functioning, and close to half (48.5%) are operating only partially. Armed violence in Haiti continues to severely disrupt access to health care, forcing numerous health facilities to close, displacing communities, and disrupting medical supply chains. The growing number of internally displaced persons (1.5 million to date) is placing additional pressure on an already overstretched health system. In 2026, an estimated 4.9 million people require health assistance. "Haiti's health system is under immense strain due to the overwhelming volume of patients and influx of trauma cases,” said Dr Tedros. “I visited Hôpital Universitaire La Paix and saw firsthand the demands facing the facility and its staff. events.summary: Country: Ukraine Source: International Atomic Energy Agency The IAEA is engaging with the Russian Federation and Ukraine on arrangements for a ninth localized ceasefire at the Zaporizhzhya Nuclear Power Plant (ZNPP) following another loss of offsite power. The plant’s connection to its sole remaining external power line, the 330 kV Ferosplavna-1 line, was lost on 25 November at 05:28 local time, reportedly due to military activity. For the 28th time during the conflict, ZNPP is relying on emergency diesel generators for essential nuclear safety and security functions. “Once again we are faced with a loss of offsite power at the ZNPP. Its continued reliance on a single power line, together with the plant’s location on the front line of an active warzone, results in an extremely precarious offsite power connection,” said IAEA Director General Rafael Mariano Grossi. “I call on both sides to work constructively with the IAEA to cease military activity against electrical infrastructure, facilitate repair of the Ferosplavna-1 line and re-establish an offsite power connection to the ZNPP,” said Director General Grossi. This event further underscores the importance of negotiations to facilitate repair of the Dniprovska 750 kV power line and its associated substation . The substation was reportedly damaged during military activity in May. The power line was repaired under the sixth Agency-negotiated temporary localized ceasefire in June, but further damage was subsequently identified. The Dniprovska substation and 750 kV line are essential components of the ZNPP's energy infrastructure. events.title: Sudan: Más de 380 000 personas desplazadas en Kordofán, Sudán, mientras la violencia obliga a miles más a huir
events.summary: Country: Sudan Source: International Organization for Migration Jartum, 26 de noviembre de 2026 – Más de 383 000 personas fueron desplazadas de la región sudanesa de Kordofán entre octubre de 2025 y octubre de 2026, mientras que la renovada inseguridad obligó a otras 15 000 personas a huir solo en noviembre. La Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) advierte que las sucesivas oleadas de desplazamiento están agravando una crisis humanitaria ya crítica, dejando a miles de familias sin alojamiento seguro, acceso a servicios básicos ni medios de subsistencia. "Las familias de todo Kordofán se ven obligadas a huir una y otra vez, mientras que las comunidades que las acogen ya tienen dificultades para satisfacer sus propias necesidades básicas", declaró Mohamed Refaat, Jefe de Misión de la OIM en Sudán. "Los civiles deben ser protegidos. A medida que más personas son expulsadas de sus hogares, necesitamos urgentemente los recursos y el acceso seguro para llegar a ellas antes de que su situación se deteriore aún más". Kordofán Occidental ha sido especialmente afectado por la última oleada de desplazamiento. Solo en noviembre, la Matriz de Seguimiento del Desplazamiento (DTM) de la OIM registró 21 incidentes de desplazamiento en toda la región, que obligaron a aproximadamente 15 310 personas a abandonar sus hogares. Casi el 90 por ciento de estos desplazamientos se originaron en Kordofán Occidental, con alrededor de 12 720 personas obligadas a huir únicamente de la localidad de Abu Zabad. Muchas familias se han visto obligadas a desplazarse en repetidas ocasiones, agotando sus ya limitados recursos e interrumpiendo el acceso a la atención sanitaria, la educación y otros servicios esenciales. events.summary: Country: Central African Republic Source: REACH Initiative Please refer to the attached file. MESSAGES CLÉS • Le coût médian du PMAS a diminué sur l’ensemble des marchés évalués avec une baisse de 10% de son prix par rapport à août. Cette tendance a été principalement observée dans la composante alimentaire, tandis que les coûts des paniers de produits non alimentaires et d’hygiène ont connu une hausse. Cependant les marchés de Bangui-Rapide, Boali et Markounda ont connu une hausse importante de leur PMAS. De manière générale, des disparités ont persisté entre les différents marchés, avec un coût médian du PMAS compris entre 40 014 XAF à Bangassou et 102 702 XAF à Dimbi. • La fonctionnalité des marchés est demeurée limitée, avec des scores SFM compris entre 51% et 88%. Cette relative stabilité a masqué des évolutions contrastées entre les différentes dimensions, marquées par une stabilité de la disponibilité des produits, un recul de l’abordabilité et une amélioration des circuits d’approvisionnement. Des améliorations des scores SFM ont été observées à Bangassou, Batangafo et Ngaoundaye, tandis que Bossangoa et Koui ont enregistré une détérioration. L’indisponibilité de certains produits et les difficultés liées à leur abordabilité ont été relevées, parallèlement à des contraintes affectant l’accessibilité des marchés et les circuits d’approvisionnement. Malgré ces évolutions, les écarts de fonctionnalité entre les marchés ont persisté, soulignant des conditions de fonctionnement et d’approvisionnement toujours hétérogènes selon les localités.

By Gifty Baah Published 26. Nov 2026 In Malawi, a farmer listening to a seasonal forecast hears that rainfall is likely to be below normal. But one important question remains unanswered: when should I plant? Plant too early and seeds may fail if the rains stop. Plant too late and crops may not reach maturity. For millions of farmers across Africa, these decisions determine whether families harvest enough food, earn an income, or face hardship. This gap between climate information and decision-making, is where NORCAP's work makes a difference. As Africa faces the impacts of the current El Niño event, NORCAP experts embedded in Regional Climate Centres and National Meteorological and Hydrological Services are contributing to transforming climate data into actionable information. Their support is strengthening forecasting systems, building technical capacity, and improving the early warnings that governments, communities and humanitarian agencies rely on to prepare for climate extremes. What is El Niño? A continent facing growing climate risk El Niño is a naturally occurring climate pattern characterised by unusually warm surface waters in the central and eastern tropical Pacific Ocean. It weakens trade winds and shifts rainfall patterns, influencing weather conditions across the globe. events.title: World: Legal Identity for Displaced People in West and Central Africa - From reform to effective access: turning political commitment into protection outcomes
events.summary: Countries: World, Burkina Faso, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Mali, Niger, Nigeria Source: Norwegian Refugee Council Please refer to the attached file. Across West and Central Africa, millions of refugees, internally displaced people and returnees are unable to obtain, replace or recover essential civil documentation. For people affected by displacement, legal identity is not simply an administrative issue. The absence of birth certificates, identity cards and other civil documents can become a humanitarian and protection concern, limiting access to assistance, education, healthcare, livelihoods, freedom of movement and other fundamental rights. It can also prevent displaced people from accessing durable solutions, including return, local integration and the recovery of housing, land and property. Drawing on research across eight countries in West and Central Africa, this NRC advocacy note examines the barriers displaced populations face in accessing legal identity and documentation. It calls on governments, donors and humanitarian and development actors to: strengthen civil registration and documentation systems in displacement-affected areas; remove legal, administrative and financial barriers that prevent displaced people from obtaining documentation; integrate legal identity more systematically into humanitarian response plans and durable solutions strategies; and invest in accessible, inclusive and long-term solutions that ensure no displaced person is left without proof of identity and legal existence. Yet they remain highly exposed to disaster risks, such as floods, fires, power outages, cyber-attacks and supply chain failures. These can disrupt operations, damage assets, cut revenues, and threaten livelihoods. Through UNDRR’s Resilient Western Balkan initiative, financed by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (AICS), the Chamber of Commerce and Industry of Serbia (CCIS) is helping MSMEs to build their disaster resilience and business continuity planning capacities. The initiative is developing a tailored package of MSME resilience tools and establishing a sustainable Business Continuity Advisory Service to train advisors nationwide to support MSMEs across the country. A workshop held on 17 November in Belgrade brought businesses, ministries and international partners together to learn about the tools and process. events.summary: Country: World Source: UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction A new model job description developed by UNDRR and the Corporate Chief Resilience Officers Network, with input from professional recruiters, helps companies establish dedicated resilience leadership and strengthen their ability to anticipate, withstand and recover from disruptions. As businesses face increasingly complex and interconnected risks, resilience can no longer be treated solely as a matter of crisis response or business continuity. It requires strategic leadership, co-ordination across business functions and clear accountability at the executive level. events.title: Japan and World Food Programme Partner to Provide Nutritious School Meals for 50,000 Young Children in Lesotho
events.summary: Countries: Lesotho, Japan Source: World Food Programme MASERU, Lesotho – The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) welcomes a JPY 200 million contribution, equivalent to USD 1.2 million, from the Government of Japan to provide nutritious school meals to 50,000 children in early childhood care and development centres across Lesotho. The contribution comes as malnutrition remains a serious concern in Lesotho, where 36 percent of children under 5 are stunted. School meals provide a vital safety net for young children, particularly in rural communities, while supporting healthier diets, regular attendance and learning. Speaking at a ceremony to announce the contribution, His Excellency Shimizu Fumio, Ambassador of Japan to Lesotho said: “For a child, a meal is about far more than simply addressing hunger. It provides the energy to learn, the nourishment to grow, and the opportunity to fully participate in school and in the community. By supporting children, we help build a healthier, stronger, and more capable future generation in Lesotho.” The funding will enable WFP to purchase 430 mt of locally sourced fortified maize meal and pulses, as well as 81 mt of canned fish, improving the quality and diversity of school meals. These foods will complement the fortified porridge provided by the Government of Lesotho. “A nutritious meal can make a lasting difference in a young child’s life,” said Anna Mukiibi-Bunnya, WFP Representative and Country Director in Lesotho. “With Japan’s generous support, thousands of children across Lesotho will have a stronger start in life and a better chance to fulfil their potential.” WFP and the Government of Lesotho currently provide two meals each day to 50,000 children aged 2 to 5 years in 2,400 early childhood care and development centres.

events.title: Humanitarian Needs and Response Trends in Northeast Nigeria, 2022-2026: A Five-Year Retrospective Analysis (November 2026)
events.summary: Country: Nigeria Source: Voices and Evidence Frontiers Please refer to the attached file. Executive Summary Over time, coordinated humanitarian response in Northeast Nigeria has progressed with minimal multi-year evidence and insight captured across annual datasets. This retrospective longitudinal analysis of secondary humanitarian datasets synthesizes five years of UNOCHA needs and planning datasets from 2022 to 2026 to extract actionable lessons for the future. An examination of needs and demographic trends reveals that the crisis remains protracted, with deep vulnerabilities persisting across total People in Need (PiN). Over the five-year period, Borno consistently remained the epicenter of the crisis, while Yobe’s caseload held steady despite tighter counting boundaries in 2026. Demographically, females consistently accounted for the majority of people in need every year, while Host Communities remained the largest share of the affected population amid declining internally displaced person (IDP) and returnee proportions. Financial and operational data further demonstrates how shrinking resource envelopes reshaped the delivery architecture. A deliberate narrowing of targeting coverage became necessary as funding shrank. Simultaneously, National NGOs (NNGOs) steadily expanded their operational share to become the primary delivery backbone as International NGOs (INGOs) drew down. Drawing on insights from the data, organizations must transition toward multi-year, cross-cutting resilience programming and diversify funding beyond traditional Humanitarian appeals.
